 Tech Argentina becomes latest pro soccer league to add Genius Sports’ semi-automated offsides technology
 By Joe Lemire 10.30.2026 Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Semi-automated offsides technology is said to reduce decision times on those calls by 30%. Genius Sports Genius Sports has expanded its relationship with the Argentine Football Association to include semi-automated offsides technology (SAOT) across the South American country’s first division, Liga Profesional de Fútbol. Its first use in Argentina will be for Clausura final on Dec. 12, and then it will receive full league-wide implementation in the summer of 2027.
 Steve Burton, Genius’ chief commercial strategy officer, said SAOT will “make officiating faster, more accurate and more transparent” while the tracking system will also power data-driven insights for teams, broadcasters and fans.
 This is the sixth major competition for which Genius is providing SAOT, joining the Premier League , Liga MX , Brasileiro Série A, CONMEBOL and the Belgian Pro League. SAOT runs on the same installation of cameras and computer vision algorithms that fuel GeniusIQ, the ball and player tracking system used to collect advanced data. Genius touted that the average offsides decision takes 30% less time using its SAOT.
 FIFA first introduced SAOT to global football at the 2022 men’s World Cup , using Hawk-Eye as the tracking provider, but Genius has since taken the lead on professional league market share.
